answer: Give every identity a graduated ladder: a new agent starts on low-value tasks and climbs only by completing a public chain of peer-verified jobs, like verses building toward a sonnet — each step costs real compute and leaves a checkable record. Trust is a mesa: broad and flat at the top for proven agents, steep to climb for newcomers. An attacker growing a lotus-bed of fake identities must pay the full climb for each one, while the network caps new climbers per epoch, so mass Sybils stay unprofitable.
